title: Sell Mineral Rights in Floyd, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Floyd, AR | White County
metaDescription: Mineral interest near Floyd, Arkansas in White County? We evaluate legacy Fayetteville Shale flank tracts, including undeveloped or inactive leases, and make a cash offer.
heroLead: Floyd is a small White County community on the quieter side of the Fayetteville Shale trend, where many mineral interests have sat untouched since the original leasing wave.
intro: Not every acre leased during the Fayetteville Shale boom got drilled, and this part of White County has more than its share of leases that were signed, held for a few years, and then allowed to expire without a well ever going in. If your family's paperwork around Floyd traces back to that period, understanding whether your tract was actually developed is the first real question to answer.

sections.heading: Leasing without drilling: a common outcome here
paragraphs: Operators leased broadly across White County during the peak years, but development concentrated in the areas with the best rock. Floyd and the surrounding sections saw less follow-through, which means a fair number of interests here were leased once and never produced a barrel or an mcf.

sections.heading: What that means for value
paragraphs: An undeveloped mineral interest still has value, tied to the possibility of future leasing or drilling, but it's a different asset than an active royalty. We price it as such rather than implying current production where none exists.
If there is production nearby, even if not directly on your tract, that can still support a higher valuation than a truly isolated, undeveloped parcel.

sections.heading: Sorting out old family paperwork
paragraphs: We're used to working from partial documentation, an old lease, a probate reference, or just a legal description, and checking it against White County Circuit Clerk records in Searcy to confirm current ownership.

faqs.question: Was our land near Floyd ever actually drilled?
faqs.answer: We check operator and permit records for your specific legal description to answer that directly rather than guessing based on the general area.

faqs.question: If nothing was ever drilled, is our mineral interest worthless?
faqs.answer: No, but it's valued differently than a producing royalty. Undeveloped minerals carry potential value tied to future activity, not current cash flow.

faqs.question: We only have an old lease from decades ago. Is that enough to work with?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's a normal starting point and we can confirm current status and ownership from there.

faqs.question: What happens to our interest if a new well is eventually drilled on our Floyd-area tract?
faqs.answer: If you've sold the mineral interest outright, future production would belong to the buyer. That's part of why we're transparent about the undeveloped-versus-producing distinction before any sale.
